passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) should be read in conjunction with the accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements, which can be found in Part II. Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data. This MD&A generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 are not included in this Form 10-K and can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II. Item 7 of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed on February 20, 2025. Company Overview Archer-Daniels-Midland Company and its subsidiaries (the "Company" or "ADM") unlocks the power of nature to enrich the quality of life. The Company is an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor, providing food security by connecting local needs with global capabilities. ADM is also a premier human and animal nutrition provider, as well as a leader in health and well-being products. Reportable Segments The Company’s operations are organized, managed, and classified into three reportable segments: Ag Services and Oilseeds, Carbohydrate Solutions, and Nutrition. The Company’s remaining operations are not reportable segments, as defined by the applicable accounting standard, and are classified within either Corporate or Other Business. See Part II. Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data. Note 17. Segment and Geographic Information for further information on the nature of our business and our reportable segments. 2025 Strategy The Company’s goal is to continue to build and sustain long-term value for its shareholders and customers. The Company has established the following priorities to help achieve its goal: • Focus on execution and cost management – ADM seeks to prioritize operational excellence and drive targeted cost reductions through: (1) boosting plant efficiencies; (2) optimizing operating leverage within the Nutrition segment; and (3) reducing third party spend and selling, general, and administrative expenses. • Strategic simplification – ADM seeks to enhance returns on invested capital by executing a pipeline of simplification opportunities to optimize our portfolio and organizational structure, including: (1) addressing performance, demand, and capacity challenges; (2) reducing capital expenditures that do not meet the Company’s return objectives; and (3) reducing capability overlaps through synergies, closures, and divestitures. • Targeted growth investment – ADM seeks to prioritize organic investment in key strategic initiatives, while also ensuring our businesses are ready for the future, including: (1) plant modernization investments; (2) cost optimization investments; and (3) enterprise system and process enhancements. • Deploy capital with discipline – ADM seeks to prudently invest in opportunities while continuing to return value to shareholders through dividends. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The risks described below, as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, should be carefully considered. Any one or more of such risks could materially and adversely affect the Company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and stock price and could cause actual results of operations and financial condition to vary materially from past or anticipated future results of operations and financial condition. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to the Company or that the Company currently believes to be immaterial may also adversely affect the Company. Operational Risks The Company is exposed to potential business disruption risks which could adversely affect the Company’s operating results and could result in increased expenses and liabilities. The Company engages in manufacturing and distribution activities across numerous markets and geographies. As a result, the Company is subject to risks inherent in such activities and from time to time has experienced unplanned downtime or extensive property damage and business disruption from various events and external factors, some of which are beyond the Company’s control. These events and factors include, but are not limited to, equipment failure, raw material shortages, natural disasters, adverse weather conditions, accidents, explosions, fires, environmental events, strikes or other labor or industrial disputes, war or acts of terrorism, cybersecurity attacks, or other unexpected outages. These events could result in personal injury, loss of life, and environmental damage. In some cases, the Company is dependent on a single plant or facility to manufacture or process certain products in a geographical region or otherwise. The Company may not be able to resolve disruptions timely or effectively, and the associated liability which could result from these risks may not always be covered by or could exceed liability insurance, and any insurance proceeds may not be received for several years after an event occurrence. The impact of these events and factors has and could in the future require significant investments and expenditures to repair damaged facilities or equipment and require management attention and other resources, which has and could adversely impact the Company’s results of operations. The Company’s operations rely on dependable and efficient transportation services, the disruption of which could result in difficulties supplying materials to the Company’s facilities and impair the Company’s ability to deliver products to its customers in a timely manner. The Company relies on access to navigable rivers and waterways in order to fulfill its transportation obligations more effectively. In addition, if certain non-agricultural commodity raw materials, such as water or certain chemicals used in the Company’s processing operations, are not available, the Company’s business could be disrupted. Any major lack of available water for use in certain of the Company’s processing operations could have a material adverse impact on operating results. credit_strengths.text: ADM's operating cash flow covers debt service comfortably, with free cash flow to debt near half of total borrowings. This strong cash generation, well above the sector median, reflects the company's essential agricultural processing and distribution operations. The cash flow tier is the strongest in the indicative profile, providing a solid buffer against earnings volatility.

The company maintains a substantial liquidity position, with unused credit lines and a current ratio above sector median. Cash and available facilities provide ample coverage for near-term maturities and working capital needs. This liquidity, combined with disciplined capital deployment, supports financial flexibility through commodity cycles.

key_risks.text: ADM's operations face significant business disruption risks, including unplanned downtime, natural disasters, and transportation interruptions. The company is dependent on single plants or facilities in some regions, and insurance may not fully cover liabilities. Such events could require substantial investments and adversely impact operating results and cash flows.

The debt maturity profile includes a notable concentration in the next twelve months and again in year five, with a large bullet maturity due in the near term. While the company has refinanced successfully in the past, a significant portion of long-term debt matures within five years, requiring ongoing access to capital markets or alternative funding sources.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage stands at approximately three times, below the sector median, indicating that operating income covers interest expense but with less headroom than peers. The company's substantial debt load and moderate operating margin contribute to this lower coverage. However, strong cash flow from operations provides a secondary source for debt service.

Free cash flow to debt is robust, exceeding the sector median, which supports the company's ability to service and repay debt. The company generated significant free cash flow after capital expenditures, which can be directed toward debt reduction or shareholder returns. This strong cash conversion underpins debt servicing capacity.

overall_credit_view.text: ADM's indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with net leverage above the sector median but within the tier two threshold. The company's strong cash flow generation and ample liquidity offset moderate leverage. However, declining operating income trend and exposure to operational disruptions warrant monitoring. The credit view is stable, supported by essential business operations.

Shareholder distributions absorb a significant portion of free cash flow, limiting debt reduction capacity. Dividends represent a substantial use of cash, while acquisitions are modest. The company's capital allocation priorities include maintaining dividends, which may constrain deleveraging. This, combined with upcoming maturities, suggests leverage will remain around current levels.

credit_strengths.text: ADM 的營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋債務償付，自由現金流對債務比率接近總借款的一半。這種強勁的現金產生能力遠高於行業中位數，反映公司不可或缺的農產品加工及分銷業務。現金流層級在指示性概況中屬最強，為盈利波動提供穩固緩衝。
公司維持充裕的流動性狀況，擁有未動用信貸額度，流動比率高於行業中位數。現金及可用融資額度為短期到期債務及營運資金需求提供充足覆蓋。此流動性結合嚴謹的資本配置，支持公司穿越商品週期的財務靈活性。

key_risks.text: ADM 的營運面臨重大業務中斷風險，包括非計劃停機、自然災害及運輸中斷。公司於部分地區依賴單一工廠或設施，保險可能無法完全覆蓋負債。此類事件可能需巨額投資，並對經營業績及現金流造成不利影響。
債務到期結構顯示未來十二個月及第五年均有顯著集中，近期有一筆大額子彈式到期債務。儘管公司過往曾成功再融資，但相當部分長期債務於五年內到期，需要持續進入資本市場或另類融資渠道。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率約為三倍，低於行業中位數，表明經營利潤可覆蓋利息支出，但緩衝空間較同業為少。公司龐大的債務負擔及中等經營利潤率導致覆蓋率較低。然而，強勁的營運現金流為債務償付提供次要來源。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，超過行業中位數，支持公司償付及償還債務的能力。公司在資本開支後產生顯著自由現金流，可用於減債或股東回報。此強勁現金轉換能力支撐債務償付能力。

overall_credit_view.text: ADM 的指示性財務風險概況為中等，淨槓桿高於行業中位數但處於第二級別門檻之內。公司強勁的現金流產生及充裕流動性抵銷中等槓桿。然而，經營利潤下降趨勢及營運中斷風險需持續監察。信貸觀點穩定，受核心業務營運支持。
股東分派吸收顯著部分自由現金流，限制減債能力。股息佔現金用途相當比重，而收購規模適度。公司的資本配置優先事項包括維持股息，可能制約去槓桿。此情況結合即將到期的債務，意味槓桿將維持於當前水平附近。
